text:
### Observed differences

- The choice between two alternative paths after A20 reversed. In the earlier window, A24, A25 and A26 each ran in about 82 in 100 traces, while A21, A22 and A23 each ran in only about 19 in 100; in the later window, A21–A23 each run in about 79 in 100 traces and A24–A26 in about 21 in 100. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007]
- A20's outgoing transitions show the same reversal directly, with A20 present in all traces in both windows: before, roughly 29%, 29% and 24% of its outgoing transitions led to A24, A26 and A25 (only about 7% and 3% to A21 and A23); after, roughly 29%, 29% and 22% led to A23, A21 and A22, with A24–A26 down to 6–8%. [DIR003, REL009]
- The two triples behave as strict alternatives with unchanged internal structure: A21–A23 never co-occur with A24–A26 in either window (before, A24 appeared without A21 in about 81 in 100 traces; after, A21 appears without A24 in about 79 in 100), and within each triple the activities occur together in both orders in similar proportions, i.e. without a fixed internal order. [REL015, REL017, REL024, REL030, REL036, REL041]
- The branch's surroundings switched with it: A30 and the pair A32/A33, which earlier typically co-occurred with A24–A26 (co-occurrence in about 82 and 52 in 100 traces), later typically co-occur with A21–A23 (about 79 and 56 in 100). [REL020, REL021, REL027, REL038, REL039, REL042, REL045]
- A10 became rarer and behaves differently: it appears in about 7 in 100 later traces versus about 17 in 100 earlier, its typical event position within the trace moved earlier and became far more variable (mean relative position about 0.86 to about 0.52), and its outgoing transitions shifted from almost only A33 (about 97%) to a spread over several activities (largest share A15, about 21%); the edge A32→A10, about 20% of A32's outgoing transitions before, is nearly unobserved after. These rest on few traces (about 33 before, 14 after). [POS001, DIR002, DIR004, REL007, REL008]
- A02 rose from about 2 to about 9 in 100 traces with a completely changed successor profile, but this rests on only 4 versus 18 observed transitions. [OCC001, DIR001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the branch choice after A20 changed: the existing alternative path through A21, A22 and A23, previously taken in about 19 in 100 traces, became the dominant route in the later window (about 79 in 100), while the path through A24, A25 and A26 dropped from about 82 to about 21 in 100. This rests on direct, fully supported successor evidence at A20 (200 traces in each window) [DIR003], on the symmetric participation swap of the six activities (each shifting by about 60 in 100 traces) [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007], and on a consistent relational picture in which the two groups are strict alternatives, keep their mixed internal order, and exchange their accompanying activities A30 and A32/A33 [REL015, REL017, REL024, REL036, REL020, REL021, REL038, REL039]. All six activities and both paths are observed in substantial shares in both windows and only the shares between the alternatives shift, which fits a change in how often existing paths are taken rather than activities being added, removed or bypassed; the many relation items largely express this one underlying shift rather than independent confirmations. Against chance, 59 control-flow items qualified where fewer than 1 would be expected without a change, and every item's difference exceeds about 995 of 1000 random re-splits of the pooled data. The evidence cannot show what determines the branch choice, and it cannot rule out that the two windows simply mix case types in different proportions; the changes around A10 and A02, based on few traces, are not established as part of this shift.

Other differences: A10 appears in fewer traces (about 17 to 7 in 100), at earlier and more variable event positions, with outgoing transitions spread over several activities instead of almost only A33; A02 appears slightly more often (about 2 to 9 in 100) with a changed successor profile. Both are based on few observations (33/14 and 4/18) and the evidence does not link them to the branch-frequency change. [POS001, DIR002, DIR004, REL007, REL008, OCC001, DIR001]
